title: Veritide Secure AI
text:
Veritide Secure AI

notes:
Summary: Veritide Secure AI is evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for a PHI + payments workload. Primary ask: full compliance mapping and an architecture that supports CMEK/HSM, strict audit logging, and US-only data residency.

Key constraints / quotes: "No persistent PHI may be processed outside of our VPC control plane need BAA before any production keys." "We require customer-managed keys (CMEK) with HSM-backed KMS and proof of key separation from Redwood control plane."

Compliance mapping (high level) requested by Veritide security:
- SOC 2 Type II: log collection (per-route/token), change control evidence, penetration test reports, SOC2 report + remediation plan.
- ISO 27001: ISMS evidence, asset inventory, supplier security controls, encryption at rest/in transit, vulnerability management cadence.
- HIPAA / BAA: BAA required; controls for PHI handling, access controls, audit trails (7+ year retention preferred), selective redaction/PII minimization in logs.
- PCI considerations: cardholder data must not be present in Redwood-managed logs; need segmentation/SCOPING guidance, SAQ A-EP guidance if using Redwood endpoints for tokenization flows.

Technical asks from Infra team:
- VPC options: private control plane with customer-managed VPC peering or PrivateLink; ability to enforce egress rules and restrict endpoints to specific subnets.
- KMS: BYOK/CMEK via AWS KMS + HSM support; key rotation policy, audit of key usage, KMS CMK ARN consumption model.
- Audit logging: support for streaming audit logs to customer S3/CloudWatch/Kinesis, immutable retention policy, ability to disable certain debug logs that may contain PII.
- Data residency: ability to pin region (us-east-1) and explicit guarantee that backups/snapshots remain in-customer project/region.
- Pen-tests & attestations: require vendor-supplied recent pen test summary and remediation list; Redwood to provide SOC2 Type II report and ISO attestation.

POC findings (brief):
- Latency/throughput: baseline meets 95th p50 for chat flows at 120ms token latency in sandbox with dedicated pool (good).
- Quality/regression: minimal model regressions; Redwood Optimize suggestions reduced token spend ~18% in test suite.
- Security: need explicit KMS integration steps; current sandbox used ephemeral keys but customer requires CMEK in production.

Decisions / open items:
- Legal requires execution of BAA before any PHI on platform. -> BLOCKER.
- Security wants vendor pen test report and a gap plan for third-party code. -> BLOCKER.
- Pricing: procurement needs committed capacity quote for Dedicated/Private and amortized KMS fees.

Next steps (actionable):
1) Redwood to deliver compliance artifacts pack (SOC2 Type II, ISO attestation, sample BAA) by 2025-02-20.
2) Schedule architecture walkthrough with Infra + Security (target week of 2025-02-24) - include KMS engineer and solutions architect.
3) Provide draft network diagram and KMS integration runbook; include steps for logging export and retention configuration.
4) Legal to review and redline BAA; procurement to approve ARR estimate.

Linked artifacts: FF-2025-01-23-0921 (call transcript), FF-2025-02-07-1145 (POC sync), Drive: Veritide-RI-Security-FAQ, Draft BAA, Jira tickets SEC-1124 / INFRA-2207.

AE notes (Maya): short, choppy CRM style - "Security happy with architecture direction; legal + procurement are slow. Customer insists on CMEK w/ HSM; if Redwood can show key separation and stream logs to their S3 with immutable retention, this will move to procurement fast. Will follow up w/ SE (Ravi) to prep design packet this week."
